metaData.originalTitle: 场景营销前端 AI Coding — AI Native 的视觉稿还原
metaData.title: Frontend AI Coding for Scenario Marketing — AI Native Visual Restoration from Design Drafts
metaData.oneSentenceSummary: This article introduces Tarot Pixel, an Agent-Native visual restoration solution: instead of generating code, it transforms design drafts into structured visual previews, allowing the Coding Agent to query on demand and implement autonomously, integrating visual restoration into the Agent's autonomous loop.
metaData.summary: Starting from the pain points of visual restoration in the AI Coding era, the article analyzes multiple structural contradictions of traditional D2C platforms: reliance on manual layer selection, image slicing, multi-state recognition, and decoupling of visual restoration from business logic. The core insight is that design drafts should enter the Agent workflow as reference materials, not as full data pushes. Tarot Pixel's design philosophy is 'Don't build a pipeline, build a library': it exports design drafts once into structured HTML previews, provides REST APIs for the Agent to query on demand—the engineering layer handles noise reduction and data extraction, while the AI layer focuses on semantic understanding. The Agent autonomously decides implementation methods within a closed loop of 'Observe → Plan → Execute → Reflect', and supports continuous conversational corrections. The article also compares two approaches—Pencil (IDE native) and Figma MCP—and emphasizes that tools should be built for AI, providing precise context in natural formats.

mainPoints.point: The essence of visual restoration is a context problem, not a code generation problem.
mainPoints.explanation: Coding Agents already have coding capabilities, but feeding raw design draft data (complex layer trees, decorative layers, multi-state artboards) directly introduces a lot of noise. Engineering-level noise reduction and on-demand querying are needed to provide clean visual context.

mainPoints.point: 'Don't build a pipeline, build a library' — design drafts should serve as reference materials, not as inputs.
mainPoints.explanation: Traditional D2C attempts to generate complete code in one go, but code without business context is unusable. Tarot Pixel lets the Coding Agent query design details on demand, with implementation done by the Agent that has full project context.

mainPoints.point: Tools should be designed for Agents, not for humans.
mainPoints.explanation: Agent tools need natural formats (prose, markdown), thorough documentation, graceful error handling, and the assumption that Agents may use them in unexpected ways—this differs from traditional API design thinking.

mainPoints.point: The Agent's autonomous loop is more valuable than one-shot generation.
mainPoints.explanation: The Agent continuously corrects within the 'Observe → Plan → Execute → Reflect' loop. Even if the first restoration is only 80% accurate, high quality can be achieved through conversational back-and-forth comparisons, meeting the dynamic needs of complex pages.

keyQuotes: Tools are made for AI to use, not for humans.
Don't build a pipeline—build a 'visual reference system' that AI can consult.
Design drafts are not inputs; they are reference materials.
The true value of an Agent lies not in generating a result in one shot, but in running its own autonomous loop of 'Observe → Plan → Execute → Reflect'.

relatedArticles.title: Harness Is Not the Goal, Knowledge Is the Moat — Knowledge Accumulation Practices of an AI Engineering Delivery Team
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Based on the engineering delivery practices of an AI Team, this article proposes that knowledge accumulation is more important than workflow orchestration, and systematically introduces a complete methodology encompassing a five-layer knowledge storage architecture, a three-level maturity system, and how workflows serve knowledge accumulation.

relatedArticles.title: Architecture Design for LLMs: What Makes a Truly AI-Friendly Architecture?
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article systematically elaborates on the three paradigms of evolution from traditional engineering architecture to AI-Friendly architecture (deterministic → probabilistic, structured → semantic, static → dynamic). It also provides a detailed explanation of core capabilities such as Multi-Agent, Context Engineering, AI-Friendly APIs, and AI Observability, using the practical implementation of AI review and Q&A systems in Taobao's flash sale business as a case study.

relatedArticles.title: Best Practices for AI Code Generation Workflows in Taobao-Tmall Marketing Backend
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article systematically summarizes the practice of the Taobao-Tmall marketing backend team in converging AI code generation from a local, decentralized model to a cloud-hosted, integrated workflow. The core methodology involves providing just enough precise knowledge, delegating deterministic logic to engineering, and establishing a positive feedback loop for knowledge.

relatedArticles.title: Investing 10,000 RMB in AI: A Year of Tools, Practices, and Reflections
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: A systematic summary of a veteran developer's practical experience in the AI wave, covering everything from MAC toolchain optimization and Harness Engineering architectural constraints to building an Agent-driven automated learning loop.

relatedArticles.title: Full-Stack RAG Technology Deep Dive
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article systematically breaks down the core technologies of the full-stack RAG pipeline from a practical perspective, covering document loading, intelligent chunking, index construction, retrieval optimization, generation tuning, advanced Graph RAG, and the Ragas automated evaluation framework, emphasizing measurable, tunable, and trustworthy engineering practices.

relatedArticles.title: AI R&D Automation: Wiki Knowledge Base + Skill Pack
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article details how to build a continuously growing team knowledge base and a supporting expert skill pack based on the LLM-Wiki model and the Obsidian platform to achieve AI-driven R&D automation.

relatedArticles.title: Harness Engineering: How I Spent a Week Boosting AI Coding Rate to 90% in an Enterprise App
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article systematically introduces Harness Engineering, a new AI coding paradigm that elevates the AI code rate of an enterprise Java application from 25% to over 90% by building a four-element system of rules, skills, knowledge, and change management.

relatedArticles.title: In-Depth Analysis of AI-Generated UI Technology: Model Streaming Output and UI Rendering Practices
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article systematically analyzes the core technologies of AI-Generated UI, focusing on the engineering practices of large language model streaming output and frontend UI rendering, covering streaming transmission protocols, mainstream open-source architectures, core challenges of streaming rendering, and AI editor implementations.

relatedArticles.title: Understanding Hermes in One Article: How the New Top-Tier Agent Self-Evolves from Experience
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article provides an in-depth analysis of the core innovation of the Hermes Agent—the Skills closed-loop system—detailing its complete implementation mechanism, from experience extraction and knowledge storage to intelligent retrieval and self-improvement, along with its engineering trade-offs and security considerations.

relatedArticles.title: Practices and Reflections on a Real-Time Inference Commodity Domain Agent at the 10,000-Level
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article details the architecture of a real-time inference commodity domain Agent built by the Taobao Commodity Center team, which adopts an event-driven, Function-Centric design. By standardizing encapsulation via AIFunction, establishing a three-tier knowledge base system, unifying online and offline workflows, and leveraging transactional domain events, the architecture enables intelligent understanding and real-time inference for hundreds of millions of products, significantly improving information completeness and R&D efficiency.
